title: Why do we brush our teeth?
examples: Teacher, what happens if I don't brush my teeth?
Are there really tiny bad things on my teeth?
How long should I brush my teeth for?

explain.say: Say, your teeth need to stay very clean to work well.

draw.text: Why do we brush our teeth?

explain.say: Say, there is a sticky film called plaque on your teeth.
say, plaque is made by tiny invisible things called germs.
say, these germs can make little holes in your teeth.
say, brushing helps to take away that sticky plaque and germs.
say, a real life example is when you eat yummy snacks.

faq.q: Why do I need to brush my teeth?
faq.a: You brush your teeth to keep them clean and strong. Plaque builds up and tiny germs can make holes in your teeth.
asks: What is the purpose of brushing?
Should I brush my teeth every day?

faq.a: Plaque is a sticky film that forms on your teeth. It is made up of germs that love to stick around.
asks: Is plaque bad for my teeth?

faq.a: Yes, germs are very tiny, much smaller than anything you can see. They are invisible to the naked eye.
You should brush for about two minutes every morning and night. This gives enough time to clean all spots.
asks: How many times a day should I brush?

faq.q: What happens if I don't brush?
faq.a: If you do not brush, plaque builds up and the germs can start making tiny holes called cavities. This can make your teeth hurt.
asks: What is the result of not brushing?

facts: Plaque is a sticky film that forms on teeth.
Germs are the tiny things that make plaque.
Brushing helps remove plaque and germs.
Brushing helps keep teeth strong and healthy.

quiz.say: What is the sticky film on your teeth?
quiz.why: Plaque is the sticky film that builds up on your teeth.

wrong.0: Germs are the things that make the plaque, not the film itself.
wrong.1: Cavities are the holes that can form later, not the film.
wrong.2: Toothpaste is what you use to clean, not the film.

quiz.say: What do germs do to teeth?
quiz.why: Germs can cause damage by making small holes in your teeth.

wrong.0: The taste is not what germs change; they cause damage.
wrong.1: Germs weaken the teeth, they do not make them stronger.
wrong.3: Making them shiny is what we want, but germs do the opposite.

quiz.say: If I brush my teeth, I am removing:
quiz.why: Brushing cleans away both the sticky plaque and the germs inside it.

wrong.1: Brushing must remove more than just the food bits left over.
wrong.2: You must remove the sticky plaque that holds the germs.
wrong.3: If you only remove plaque, the germs will still be there.
